witness.text:
The person who owns it is very
likely part of the 79% who have already
reached the seven-figure milestone

comparisons.rationale: Ramsey's 79% is the share of millionaires who received no inheritance, not the share of old-car owners who are millionaires, and it does not mean "built wealth from nothing" (no inheritance is not the same as no help); the sentence turns a statistic about millionaires into a probability about a stranger's car.
comparisons.uncertainty: The 79% no-inheritance figure was confirmed from search-result summaries; the inference drawn from it is the analyst's reading.

witness.text:
Just a 5-year delay from age 35 to 40
costs you more than $269,000

comparisons.rationale: $500 a month at 8% reaches $1.745M from 25, $745K from 35 and $476K from 40; the 35-to-40 gap is $270K and the 25-to-40 gap is $1.27M, all as stated.
comparisons.uncertainty: Arithmetic verified (monthly compounding).

witness.text:
It's 15
separate years each carrying that same
cost stacked on top of one another

comparisons.rationale: Each missed year does not carry "that same cost": the first missed year costs about $139,500, but later years cost less because they have less time to compound (the 15 years sum to $1.27M, about $85,000 on average).
comparisons.uncertainty: Arithmetic verified.

witness.text:
Double your savings rate and you double
your outcome and actually more than
double it because of compound growth

comparisons.rationale: The video's own numbers ($594,000 at 10% and $1,189,000 at 20%) are exactly double; the outcome is linear in the savings rate for a fixed return, so "more than double" is wrong.
comparisons.uncertainty: Arithmetic verified.

witness.text:
grows
into approximately $785,000

comparisons.rationale: The $785,000 is reproduced only if all seven half-raises ($1,500-$3,000) are invested for the full 20 years (about $720,000 annual or $773,000 monthly at a $2,250 midpoint; $785,000 needs an average of about $2,285); one raise a year to a common end gives about $540,000-$576,000 and one every two years about $409,000, and the script does not state the timing.
comparisons.uncertainty: Arithmetic verified under stated timing assumptions; raise timing is not given.

witness.text:
means giving up
approximately $368,000

comparisons.rationale: $625 a month at 8% for 20 years is about $368,100; the wording "investment growth" is loose, since this is the full balance, of which $150,000 is contributions.
comparisons.uncertainty: Arithmetic verified.

witness.text:
costs
approximately $78,000
in lost growth alone

comparisons.rationale: $78,000 equals three years of 8% growth on the existing $300,000 ($77,900), which is still earned if the balance stays invested; the loss from a caregiving break is the growth on the contributions not made, which is not given.
comparisons.uncertainty: Arithmetic verified.

witness.text:
the average equity investor earned
only about 5.5% per year while the S&P
500 returned approximately 9.9%

comparisons.rationale: The attributed DALBAR 2024 figures could not be matched to a source; the 5.5-point gap resembles a single-year gap, not a per-year long-run difference, and DALBAR's method is contested.
comparisons.uncertainty: No source located for the 5.5% and 9.9%.

witness.text:
In 2025 alone, the US
created an additional 736,000
new millionaires

comparisons.rationale: Capgemini's World Wealth Report 2026 reports 736,000 new US millionaires in 2025 (US population of high-net-worth individuals 8.7 million), but the same passage cites 23.8 million and 14.5 million "millionaires" on other definitions, and Capgemini's own investable-asset measure for the US is far below 14.5 million; the three bases are not reconciled.
comparisons.uncertainty: Verified from search-result summaries of Capgemini releases; the other counts are unsourced in the video.

witness.text:
effectively owns about 1,875,000
in future earnings

comparisons.rationale: $75,000 times 25 years is $1.875M undiscounted and without raises; its present value at a 3% discount rate is about $1.31M, so "owns $1,875,000" overstates the asset.
comparisons.uncertainty: Arithmetic verified.

witness.text:
After 30 years, you'll surpass

comparisons.rationale: 15% of $75,000 invested monthly at 8% gives $171,500, $552,200 and $1,397,200 at 10, 20 and 30 years, matching the stated figures (monthly compounding, no raises); the other savings-rate comparison ($1,699,000 versus $850,000) uses annual contributions, a different convention.
comparisons.uncertainty: Arithmetic verified.

financial_checks.claim: Starting at 26 instead of 25 costs "$139,521"; the 15 missed years "each carr[y] that same cost"
financial_checks.result: First missed year about $140,000 (holds); later years cost progressively less, so the "same cost" claim is wrong.

financial_checks.claim: $75,000 income, save 10% or 20% for 25 years at 8%: $594,000 and $1,189,000; "more than double"

financial_checks.result: $1.699M and $0.850M with annual contributions (monthly would be $1.863M and $0.932M); consistent ratio, different convention from the $500/month examples.

financial_checks.claim: Seven raises of $3,000-$6,000, half invested at 8% for 20 years, "approximately $785,000"
financial_checks.result: About $720,000-$773,000 if all seven half-raises are invested for the full 20 years; $540,000-$576,000 if one raise a year; $409,000 if every two years. Timing is not stated.

financial_checks.claim: $625/month at 8% for 20 years is "approximately $368,000"; $1,000 from 25 is $21,725 and from 40 is $6,848
A 3-year caregiving break on a $300,000 portfolio at 8% costs "$78,000 in lost growth"
financial_checks.result: $77,900 is the 3-year growth on the existing balance, not growth lost by missing contributions.

financial_checks.claim: Automatic plans 12.1% versus 7.6% savings: 4.5 points of $75,000 over 25 years at 8% is "$267,476"
financial_checks.result: $267,500 with monthly contributions; arithmetic holds. The cause attributed to automation is not controlled for who enrols.

financial_checks.claim: $75,000 for 25 years is "about 1,875,000 in future earnings"
financial_checks.result: Undiscounted; present value at 3% is about $1.31M.

Capgemini World Wealth Report 2026 (via search-result summaries): US added 736,000; US HNWI population 8.7 million. The video's 23.8M / 14.5M / 6M bases are not Capgemini's. (search-result summaries only)

financial_checks.claim: 79% of millionaires had no inheritance; only 3% inherited $1M or more; only 16% over $100,000
financial_checks.result: Ramsey Solutions National Study of Millionaires (search-result summaries): 79% no inheritance, 3% received $1M+; the 16% figure was not located. The "built wealth from nothing" gloss is stronger than the data. (search-result summaries only)

financial_checks.claim: Ohio State divorce study: 77% decline in net worth; medical bankruptcy "the leading cause"; Vanguard 2026 12.1% vs 7.6%; DALBAR 5.5% vs 9.9%; disability insurance 1-2% of income; millionaires' home equity 19% of assets
financial_checks.result: Not re-verified; the medical-bankruptcy claim is contested in the literature and the DALBAR pair could not be matched.

strengths: Clear structure and unusually precise compounding examples, most of which reproduce.
Concrete actions and a well-placed end CTA.
Explains avalanche versus the freed-payment redirect, which is the useful behavioural step.
weaknesses: The 79% statistic is misapplied in the hook and glossed as "from nothing".
Three arithmetic or logic errors in the barrier section ("same cost", "more than double", $785,000 timing).
Thumbnail lineup not in the script.
Very long for one video (~18,500 characters).
contradictions: "Each carrying that same cost" versus the declining cost of later missed years.
"Double ... and actually more than double" versus $594,000 to $1,189,000.
"Millionaires" at 23.8M, 14.5M and 6M versus Capgemini's 8.7M US HNWI on an investable basis.
"25 to 30 years" from "a few hundred dollars a month" versus the video's own $500/month reaching $745,000 at 30 years ($1 million takes about 33 years).
improvement_opportunities: Reword the hook to "79% of millionaires received no inheritance" and drop the old-car inference.
Show the 25-to-40 delay as a table of years versus cost (first year $140K shrinking) instead of "the same cost".
Replace the thumbnail lineup with a figure from the script (the $500/month 25-versus-35 comparison) or add the Mike example to the video.
Fix the "more than double" line and state raise timing or use $540,000.
